chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Muawiya was the first to hang two shutters on his door in Makkah.'
So he prevented the pilgrims of the House of Allah from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Equal is the one who dwells in it and the one who visits it.'
And the people, when they arrived in Makkah, the visitor would lodge with the dweller until he fulfilled his Hajj.
And Muawiya was the owner of the chain of which Allah the Exalted spoke: 'A chain whose length is seventy cubits, thrust him into it.'
'Surely he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent,' and he was the Pharaoh of this community.

key_terms.حَاجَّ بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: Pilgrims of the House of Allah
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَة: Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, the Umayyad Caliph

ai.seo_question: Who was the Pharaoh of this Ummah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Muawiya as the first to install double doors on the Ka'bah, a structural change that symbolized the Umayyad monopolization of religious authority and the exclusion of the common pilgrim. This act is theologically linked to the 'chain of seventy cubits' in Surah al-Haqqa, casting Muawiya as the 'Pharaoh of this Ummah' who bound the people to his rule, a concept deeply resonant in Shia historiography regarding the shift from communal access to dynastic control.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muawiya was the first one to hang two shutters upon his door in Makkah.
So he prevented the Pilgrims of the House of Allahazwj from what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [22:25] They are equal in it, the dweller and the visitor.
And the people, when they used to come to Makkah, the visitor would lodge with the dweller until he had fulfilled his Hajj,
but Muawiya is an owner of the chains which Allahazwj the Exalted Speaks of in [69:32] Then thrust him into a chain the length of which is seventy cubits,
therefore chain him [69:33] Surely he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent, and he was the Pharaohla of this community’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following:
“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Mu‘awiyah was the first person who built door-jambs for his house in Makkah
and prevented the pilgrims to the House of Allah to use it, against the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Both resident and nonresident have equal right to use it.’ [22:24]
The people arriving in Makkah, who were not residents, would stay with residents until the end of Hajj season.
Mu‘awiyah was the person of the chains about which Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, has said, ‘With the chain which is seventy yards long, (you must) chain him;
He did not believe in Allah, the Great.’ (69:31-32) He was the pharaoh of this nation.’”
